objectives: Identify rimes in taught pl-words and familiar CVC partners.
Group words that share the vowel and ending sounds.
Distinguish words that share pl but have different rimes.
Decode each word fully after sorting.
concepts: A word family shares a rime, not necessarily an onset.
Pl-words such as plan, plug, plum, plot and plop have different rimes.
CVC partners such as man, mug, gum, hot and top make the rime pattern visible.
Word-family sorting supports decoding but does not replace it.

definitions.definition: Words that share a rime, such as plan and man with -an.
The vowel and sounds that follow it in a syllable.
The initial consonant sound or group before the vowel.

workedExamples.solution: They share -an; plan has onset pl and man has onset m.
Both begin pl and have short /o/, but plot ends /t/ and plop ends /p/.

commonMistakes: Grouping words by onset instead of rime.
Treating all pl-words as one family.
Ignoring the final consonant when sorting.
Guessing from the family label rather than decoding the full word.
keyTakeaways: Compare the vowel and ending to identify a rime.
Words with the same onset can have different rimes.
Words with different onsets can share a rime.
Decode the whole word after sorting.
revisionPoints: plot and hot share -ot; plop and top share -op.

basic.prompt: What is the rime in plug?

conceptual.prompt: What makes plan and man a word-family pair?
Do plot and plop share a rime?
conceptual.answer: No; they share pl but have -ot and -op.

conceptual.prompt: Why should you decode after sorting?
conceptual.answer: The family pattern helps but does not replace reading the whole word.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How are plug and mug alike and different?
higherOrderThinking.answer: They share -ug; plug has onset pl and mug has onset m.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why are plan and plug in different rime groups?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Their vowel and ending differ: -an and -ug.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: What should you do if a word does not sound like its family?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Decode it again and check every grapheme.

mixedReview.prompt: What is the onset in plum?
What does a word-family sort help you notice?
mixedReview.answer: Shared rimes and differences among words

activities.name: Sort pl-words by rime.
steps: Read plan, plug, plum, plot and plop.
Pair each with a familiar CVC word sharing its rime.
Name the onset and rime in each word.
Read every word again to confirm the sort.

activities.name: Compare pl-words with similar rimes.
steps: Contrast plot/plop to hear the ending difference.
Explain why the onset alone cannot identify the word.

outcomes: Identify onset and rime in taught pl-words.
Explain differences among pl-words with the same onset.
Decode the full word after sorting.

answerKeys.explanation: Plan and man both end in -an.
Plot has onset pl and rime -ot.
Both begin pl but have different rimes.
The vowel and ending distinguish pl-words.
Plug and mug share -ug but have different onsets.
Full decoding confirms the word and the sort.
